small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs that tile the OC dimension too (e.g. BLOCK_OC=8/16 with BLOCK_N=64/128/256) so smaller BLOCK_N tiles don't waste the 16-wide OC accumulator; current kernel forces OC_C=16 which limits register reuse vs. BLOCK_N tradeoffs.
- Pre-load all 81 weights into registers once per program (small static array of OC×K_TOTAL = 16×81 = 1296 fp32 = ~5KB) before the spatial loop, so the inner loop only does input gathers and FMAs — currently each of 81 iters re-issues a 16-elem weight load.
- Try tiling over (n, od) into BLOCK_D groups so the same kh/kw row of the input is reused across multiple od values (input depth reuse via shared kd indexing), and add configs with num_stages=3-4 at BLOCK_N=128 with num_warps=8.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM layout where the program tiles (BLOCK_M over OC) × (BLOCK_N over N*OD*OH*OW) and reduces over K=IC*KD*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=27 or 81; use tl.dot on fp32/tf32 to leverage tensor cores instead of the current outer-product accumulation, which is FMA-bound and underutilizes the 4090.
- Consider a channels-last (NDHWC) input layout transform once per forward so the GEMM-K (IC*kd*kh*kw) gathers become coalesced contiguous loads along IC; the current NCDHW layout strides IC by ID*IH*IW which hurts L1 reuse.
- Alternative: persistent-CTA design where each SM owns a slice of output spatial tiles and streams weights once into shared memory, fusing the scale/tanh/bias/sigmoid epilogue exactly as today — amortizes weight traffic across many output tiles per CTA.
